question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0018’s opt-in canonical readiness contract, including `gateway.readiness`, required/advisory conditions, and activation-scoped plugin providers, independently of the separate hosting-profile proposal?
rationale: The documentation is intentionally asking for durable public configuration and plugin-contract choices; source review cannot determine whether those are the product boundaries maintainers want to support.

options.title: Sponsor the readiness contract
options.body: Approve the opt-in readiness direction as the reusable foundation, while requiring linked implementation work to preserve the documented legacy path and prove the final runtime behavior.

options.title: Keep the RFC draft pending product review
options.body: Leave this PR open until a maintainer explicitly confirms the activation, aggregation, and plugin-provider boundaries before publishing them as an RFC contract.

options.title: Narrow or defer the proposal
options.body: Request a smaller RFC that documents only the existing Gateway checker and postpone new configuration and plugin-provider contracts until the owning runtime design is settled.

recommendation.title: Keep the RFC draft pending product review
recommendation.body: Leave this PR open until a maintainer explicitly confirms the activation, aggregation, and plugin-provider boundaries before publishing them as an RFC contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They have carried the RFC’s revisions and the related readiness proposal context, making them the best available routing contact for obtaining the missing maintainer decision.
